watch: Sales growth ~10% a year over 5 years

ratio.name: ROCE
ratio.explain: Profit earned on every ₹100 put to work in the business

script.title: THE FACE-OFF
lines: TCS and Infosys. India's two largest IT services companies.
Together they're worth over 13.5 lakh crore rupees, and both have fallen more than 20 percent in the last year.
So how do they really compare? Let's go through the numbers, one by one.

script.title: SIZE
lines: On size, TCS has a market cap of 8.8 lakh crore. Infosys, 4.6 lakh crore.
TCS also earns about 2.67 lakh crore in yearly revenue, around 1.5 times Infosys.

script.title: SHARE PRICE
lines: The share price has had a tough stretch for both.
Over one year, TCS is down 22 percent, and Infosys 24 percent.
Even over five years, both have returned around minus 7 to minus 8 percent a year.
Only the ten-year view is positive: about 9 percent a year for TCS, and 10 for Infosys.
Today, TCS trades 27 percent below its 52-week high. Infosys, 34 percent below.

script.title: VALUATION
lines: Here's what you pay for each.
TCS trades at 16.2 times earnings. Infosys, at 14.7.
On book value, TCS is at 7.4 times, Infosys at 4.7.
And Infosys pays a higher dividend yield: 4.2 percent, versus 2.6 for TCS.

script.title: REVENUE GROWTH
lines: Since financial year 2017, TCS grew revenue from 1.18 lakh crore to 2.67 lakh crore.
Infosys grew faster, from 68 thousand crore to 1.79 lakh crore.
Over ten years, that's about 9 percent a year for TCS, and 11 for Infosys.

script.title: PROFIT GROWTH
lines: On profit, TCS earned 49 thousand crore last year. Infosys, 29 thousand crore.
Ten-year profit growth is about 8 percent a year for both.

script.title: LAST 8 QUARTERS
lines: Over the last eight quarters, both have kept revenue rising.
TCS reached 73 thousand crore in the September quarter. Infosys, 49 thousand crore.
Operating margins are steady: around 26 to 27 percent for TCS, and 24 for Infosys.

script.title: EFFICIENCY
lines: Return on capital employed shows how much profit each rupee in the business earns.
TCS has lifted it from 44 percent to 63 percent over ten years.
Infosys improved too, from 30 to 40 percent. Both are strong, but TCS is far ahead.

script.title: CASH & DIVIDENDS
lines: Profits matter most when cash actually comes in.
Last year, TCS generated 52 thousand crore in operating cash, more than its net profit.
Infosys generated 34 thousand crore, also above its profit.
Both return most of it. TCS paid out 81 percent of profit as dividends. Infosys, 66 percent.

script.title: WHO OWNS IT
lines: Tata Sons holds about 72 percent of TCS, unchanged for two years.
Infosys promoters hold just 14 percent. Domestic institutions, like mutual funds and insurers, own the biggest share, at nearly 43 percent.
One shared trend: foreign investors have been selling both, while domestic institutions keep buying.

script.title: LATEST QUARTER
lines: The latest quarter covers July to September 2026.
TCS grew revenue 11 percent and profit 15 percent from a year ago, and signed 9.6 billion dollars of new deals.
Infosys grew revenue nearly 11 percent and profit 6 percent. Its large-deal wins hit 5.2 billion dollars.
But Infosys also cut its full-year growth guidance, to 1 to 2 percent in constant currency.

script.title: STRENGTHS & WATCH-OUTS
lines: So, what are the strengths, and what should you watch?
TCS: top-tier return ratios, strong cash generation, and steady margins. The watch-outs: slower sales growth, and a high price to book.
Infosys: a lower valuation, a higher dividend yield, and faster long-term growth. The watch-outs: the guidance cut, and low promoter holding.

script.title: THE SUMMARY
lines: TCS is the bigger, more efficient company, with a stable owner.
Infosys is cheaper, pays a higher yield, and has grown a little faster.
This is not a buy or sell call. Which one suits your style? Tell us in the comments.
